web_blocks.title: What Kross Limited Does & What Our November 2026 Refresh Uncovered

web_blocks.html: Kross Limited (NSE: KROSS) makes forged parts for heavy trucks, tractors, and extruded trailer axles in Jamshedpur [1][2]. Trailer axles reached 49% of Q2 FY27 sales (~₹115 Cr, +55% YoY volume) [29]. That lifted Q2 sales +79.6% YoY to ₹235.1 Cr and PAT +143.5% YoY to ₹19.69 Cr [3][30]. Yet our November 2026 Pass 1 audit found three sharp balance-sheet strains. First, H1 FY27 CFO fell to ₹4.73 Cr on ₹33.16 Cr PAT (14.3% conversion) after a ₹23.89 Cr jump in Other Current Assets [30]. That produced -₹54.43 Cr H1 FCF on top of -₹111 Cr across FY24–FY26 [11][30]. Second, gross debt (₹119 Cr in Sep 2026) is guided to ~₹165–170 Cr by March 2027 [29]. That funds ~₹110 Cr H2 capex and a new ₹20–25 Cr Cold Drawn Tube line [29]. Meanwhile, the Oct 30 preferential issue brought only ₹39.75 Cr upfront, with ₹23.85 Cr tied to 18-month promoter warrants across 6.75 Cr diluted shares [32]. Third, selling ~50% non-captive output from 1,20,000 TPA Mill 219 pits Kross against a 93%-share domestic oligopoly (Maharashtra Seamless, Jindal SAW, Kirloskar Ferrous/ISMT) [31]. Business quality stays CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (`PASS_WITH_WATCH`).

web_blocks.html: On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close, Kross traded at ₹277.00 [33]. Price stays in primary Stage 2 (+18.32% above 30W SMA ₹226.59) on dry volume (0.21x 30D avg) [33]. Still, it sits below its 50-DMA (₹272.34) with weak 4H RSI (35.22, `intraday_4h_turn: false`) and no NSE F&O chain (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`) [33]. In our 2026-11-23 Zerodha ledger, our stake grew to 424 shares at ₹273.05 avg cost (₹1,15,773.60 total). Market value is ₹1,17,448.00 at ₹277.00 (+1.45%, 2.75% weight) and ₹1,13,674.40 (-1.81%) at ₹268.10. Our holding action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP (`holding_shares_to_sell = 0`). We ratchet the hard stop upward from ₹212.00 to ₹219.06 across all 424 shares. Reflecting Pass 1 debt and oligopoly risks, we trim our Base Target from ₹400.00 to ₹360.00 (24.0x FY28E diluted EPS ₹14.96). New capital stays WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (`TIER_3`) in ₹234.00–₹252.00 (3.28:1 R:R from ₹252.00 vs. 1.43:1 at ₹277.00 NSE and 1.87:1 at ₹268.10 live TV).

web_blocks.takeaway: Kross’s Q2 FY27 earnings surge is real, yet 14.3% H1 cash conversion and ~₹165–170 Cr projected debt cap valuation at ₹360.00. Hold our 424 Zerodha shares with a ratcheted ₹219.06 stop and wait for ₹234.00–₹252.00 (3.28:1 R:R) before committing fresh capital.

web_blocks.html: Across all three investment horizons, our discipline is consistent. Short-term traders face an unconfirmed 4-hour pullback below the 50-DMA (₹272.34) with no NSE F&O options chain [33]. Medium-term buyers should wait for structural support inside ₹234.00–₹252.00 (3.28:1 R:R from ₹252.00) paired with Q3 FY27 cash-conversion improvement or on-schedule Mill 219 trials [29][30]. Long-term compounders must wait for sustained positive free cash flow and ROCE above 20% before upgrading conviction [1][30].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional dossier on Kross Limited. Before we walk through five Jamshedpur plants, newly audited H1 FY27 cash flows, and multi-timeframe stock charts, let me place the updated verdict and exact portfolio rules right on the table.

Kross Limited remains a credible, backward-integrated Tier-1 supplier of forged truck and tractor components and single-piece extruded trailer axles. Its trailer business reached 49% of Q2 FY27 sales, driving a 79.6% year-over-year revenue jump to ₹235.1 Cr and a 143.5% profit surge to ₹19.69 Cr. Yet our November 2026 forensic refresh uncovered heavier balance-sheet strains than our prior edition captured: H1 FY27 unaudited operating cash flow collapsed to just ₹4.73 Cr (14.3% of PAT), H1 free cash flow hit -₹54.43 Cr, gross debt is guided to ~₹165–170 Cr by March 2027, the October 30 preferential issue brought only ₹39.75 Cr upfront, and Kross must sell half of its 1,20,000 TPA Mill 219 seamless-tube output against a 93%-share domestic oligopoly. Business quality stays CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL.

Meanwhile, our portfolio stake has grown significantly. In our verified November 23, 2026 Zerodha ledger, we hold 424 shares at an average cost of ₹273.05 (₹1,15,773.60 cost basis, ₹1,17,448.00 market value at the November 23 NSE close of ₹277.00, 2.75% portfolio weight; mark-to-market ₹1,13,674.40 or -1.81% at the November 25 live TradingView close of ₹268.10). We retain all 424 shares under HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP (0 shares to sell now), ratchet our hard stop upward from ₹212.00 to ₹219.06, trim our Base Target from ₹400.00 to ₹360.00, and keep our new-capital verdict at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_3) in ₹234.00–₹252.00 (3.28:1 R:R from ₹252.00) while holding 100% of marginal ₹1,00,000 cash in reserve.

book_subsections.title: How to Read This Refreshed Monograph
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 were audited strictly price-blind before we touched a single live stock quote. In this refresh, we patched Chapters 3, 4, 5, and 6 directly with our Pass 1 discoveries from the verbatim October 22, 2026 Q2 FY27 earnings call transcript, the October 17 H1 FY27 unaudited cash flow statement, the October 30 preferential warrant structure, and the October 23 DGTR seamless-pipe sunset review. Chapters 7 through 9 then re-anchor valuation, inspect the dual-date Stage 2 chart (November 23 NSE ledger close ₹277.00 versus November 25 live TradingView close ₹268.10), and set our binding portfolio rules.

Notice why this two-stage discipline protects your capital when a stock pulls back 12.5% in a month. Without the Pass 1 forensic audit, a drop from ₹305.90 to ₹268.10 might look like a routine bargain right inside our old ₹268–₹282 buy zone. Once you see that H1 operating cash flow fell to ₹4.73 Cr, March 2027 debt is heading toward ₹170 Cr, and we already own 424 shares (2.75% portfolio weight), the right move becomes crystal clear: do not average down into an unconfirmed 4-hour dip.

Instead, let your existing 424 shares work inside the primary Stage 2 uptrend while protecting them with a tighter, upward-ratcheted ₹219.06 hard stop. Keep 100% of fresh marginal capital in cash until price either tests our deeper ₹234.00–₹252.00 demand zone with a confirmed 4-hour turn and Q3 FY27 cash-conversion proof, or proves via clean February–March 2027 Mill 219 trials that free cash flow is finally ready to turn positive.

Keep one overarching principle in mind as you read forward: operating momentum in Jamshedpur can lift quarterly revenue rapidly, yet only cash conversion and disciplined balance-sheet leverage turn a cyclical surge into lasting shareholder wealth. This monograph gives you every number, peer multiple, and chart trigger needed to hold Kross calmly without ever crossing into FOMO.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why We Refused to Auto-Buy the Old Zone
book_callouts.quote: A lower stock price is only a better entry if the forensic audit confirms the balance sheet stayed just as clean as you first thought.
book_callouts.text: When Pass 1 revealed 14.3% H1 cash conversion, ~₹165–170 Cr projected debt, and a 93% seamless-tube oligopoly, we trimmed our Base Target to ₹360.00, lowered our support entry zone to ₹234.00–₹252.00, and ratcheted our 424-share stop up to ₹219.06.
